subject: Dedicated capacity: deposit & phase schedule clarification
messages:
From: Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@oliveai.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity deposit & ramp questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the pricing packet — procurement had a couple of follow-ups before we escalate to legal/finance. Two quick asks: 1) can you confirm the required upfront deposit for a 12-month vs 24-month reserved commit (we saw a range listed but need a single % confirmed), and 2) our product team wants to push the capacity start by ~30 days to align with a rollout. If we delay the start, does the deposit change and do you provide throughput guarantees from day 1 of the committed start?

Also, can you send the worksheet that maps GPU pool sizing to target throughput (reqs: 150 requests/sec at 512 tokens avg)? We want to validate your sizing assumptions.

Appreciate a short answer today if possible — procurement is on a tight cadence.

Best,
Hector
Olive AI — Head of Procurement
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@oliveai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity deposit & ramp questions

Hector — thanks, quick answers below and I attached the capacity worksheet + draft terms. Attaching: RDW-Dedicated-Terms-OliveAI-v1.pdf, capacity-worksheet-oliveai.xlsx

Short answers:
- Deposit: our standard is 20% for 12-month, 15% for 24-month, 10% for 36-month (deposit applied to first invoice; refundable credits tied to usage thresholds).
- If you delay the start date (within 90 days of signature) we can either 1) push invoices and keep deposit %, or 2) offer to amortize the deposit across first 3 invoices if you need cashflow relief — we can mark that in the SOW.
- Throughput guarantees: we provide an availability SLA and throughput SLO tied to reserved pool size. Guarantees are effective from the committed start date. If you want an earlier soft-guarantee during staging, we can offer a reduced throughput SLO (e.g., 80% of target) until full capacity is live.

Proposed next steps (pick one):
1) Sign 24-month: 15% deposit, start 2026-08-01, phased ramp to full capacity over 6 weeks.
2) Sign 12-month: 20% deposit, start 2026-08-15, phased ramp over 8 weeks, slightly higher unit price.
3) Custom: we can do 24-month with 18% deposit + invoice schedule (month 1 partial), if procurement needs lower upfront.

I've looped in Marissa (AE) for commercial and Dev (SE) for sizing verification — he will confirm the worksheet numbers. If you want, I can prepare a DocuSign with option 3 so procurement can approve quickly.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sales, Redwood Inference

Hannah — thanks for the clarity. Procurement preference is to minimize upfront cash: can you do 12-month with 12% deposit (instead of 20%) if we commit to a strict minimum MRR and pay the remainder across months 1–3? Also two nitty items: 1) we need a written SLA around throughput (not just availability) with credit tiers if throughput falls below agreed baseline; 2) if we delay start to 2026-09-01, will that require re-risking the price (we’d like price protection).

We can move fast on a 12-month if terms are agreeable; otherwise we’ll consider the 24-month option.

-Hector
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity deposit & ramp questions — Olive AI counter

Internal — Olive is pushing for a low up-front deposit (12%) on a 12-month and wants SLA credits for throughput. Also asking that pricing be protected if start slips to 1 Sep. Can we do this without exposing us too much? Specific asks:
- Is 12% deposit acceptable if we require the rest to be invoiced months 1–3 and secured by PO?
- Can SE quantify the pool headroom needed to guarantee 150 req/s @512 tokens (p99 targets) and whether we can build a throughput-credit schedule?
- Finance: if we allow delayed start + price hold, what risk does this create for capacity planning (revenue recognition / forecasting)?

Marissa — can you own negotiating the DocuSign variant (12% deposit + invoice schedule) if SE/Finance sign off? Need answer EOD tomorrow.

Thanks, Hannah
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity deposit & ramp questions — Olive AI counter

Hannah / team — technical summary and recommendation:
- Sizing: to reliably meet 150 r/s at ~512 tokens average and maintain p99 latency under 600ms, we recommend a reserved pool equivalent to 8 x A100-class GPUs with continuous KV caching and 256-token KV headroom pre-warmed. I captured the calc in the attached capacity-worksheet-oliveai.xlsx (tab: 150rps_512t).
- Throughput SLOs: we can offer a throughput SLO expressed as baseline throughput (150 r/s) with credit tiers: 0–5% shortfall => no credit, 5–20% => 10% credit of monthly fee for the dedicated pool, >20% => 30% credit + escalation. Credits are only payable if Redwood is at fault (not due to customer traffic spikes beyond agreed burst policy).
- Ramp: propose staged ramp over 6 weeks (30% / 60% / 100%) for the 24-month case; for 12-month we can do 8 weeks but require a slightly higher deposit or the invoice amortization plan.
- Start date hold: we can lock price for up to 60 days from signature if PO in place; beyond that we need a tiered reprice (market index) to protect against cloud/GPU cost swings.

Recommendation: accept 12% deposit only if procurement signs a PO that secures the remaining commit (months 1–3 invoiced) and we include the throughput SLO + credit tiers above. Otherwise push for 15% for 24-month or amortized deposit for 12-month.

Attaching the worksheet.
-Dev
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity deposit & ramp questions — final commercial option

Hector — appreciate the constructive back-and-forth. Based on SE/Finance input we can do an approvalable commercial path that balances your procurement needs and Redwood’s capacity risk. Summary offer below (one-page commercial summary; full terms attached):

Offer (preferred): 24-month reserved commit
- Unit: Reserved pool equivalent of 8 x A100-class GPUs (as per attached worksheet) to meet 150 r/s @512 tokens.
- Price: 15% list discount (annualized pricing in attached terms).
- Deposit: 18% of first-year committed value, applied to first invoice. If Olive meets agreed monthly usage thresholds for the first 6 months, 50% of the deposit is returned as account credit.
- Start date: 2026-08-15 (we can move to 2026-09-01 if PO issued by 2026-07-20 — price protection window).
- Ramp: 6-week phased ramp (30% / 60% / 100%). During ramp we provide a soft throughput SLO at 80% of baseline; full throughput SLO (150 r/s) is effective once pool is at 100% and in production for 72 hours.
- Throughput credits: 5–20% shortfall => 10% credit of monthly pool fee; >20% => 30% credit + remediation plan. Credits are only paid when issue is attributable to Redwood.
- Invoice schedule: standard monthly invoices; we can amortize the deposit across months 1–3 if you provide PO that guarantees payment.

If you prefer a 12-month contract we can do that at higher unit rates and an 20% deposit (or 12% deposit with PO securing month 1–3 payments).

Next steps: I can generate a DocuSign with the 24-month option and the alternate 12-month lane (for procurement to sign). Link: https://docusign.net/somewhere/ID-7f3b2. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/RDW-3241.

Please advise which lane you want to move forward on and I’ll have Marissa prep the contract.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sales, Redwood Inference
